blocking.raised_by: Codex, escalating what this receipt had declared as a non-blocking give-back limitation
blocking.summary: The give-back restores kind and text but never re-runs classification, so restored lines keep fenced=False. Under the repair's own policy an unterminated comment encloses nothing, which makes those lines literal text - and literal text containing a fence should be classified as a fence.

blocking.why_it_blocks: a heading textually inside a valid fence becomes the indexed title - the highest-weighted FTS column and a line printed verbatim to the model - and fence markers the cleanup exists to remove reach the indexed body. It is the same title-promotion class this package exists to close, reached through the give-back rather than the fence parser.
blocking.why_the_previous_defence_fails: this receipt argued 'the title and the chunk bodies agree, so nothing the pipeline removed reaches the model'. Agent C accepted that. Codex is right that it does not resolve the defect: the contract is that a heading inside a fence is not a heading, and after give-back the fence is real, so the classification is simply wrong.

escalation.root_cause: The give-back exists because classification decides a line's fate before it knows whether the comment that claimed it ever closes. It patches that by undoing the text, but it cannot undo the STATE the wrong decision produced - fence tracking already ran with those lines swallowed. Every fix in this package has been correct about text and silent about state.

recommended_next.description: Make classification two-pass. First scan the note to find which '<!--' openers actually close; then classify once, treating an unterminated opener as literal text FROM THE START. Fence state is then computed over the real line set and the give-back disappears entirely, along with its whole class of state bugs. This is the smallest change that removes the cause rather than the symptom.

Stop hand-rolling a Markdown block parser. Ten attempts have now failed at: a regex spanning lines, cleanup over fenced content, per-chunk fence state, fence-before-comment precedence, a give-back restoring the wrong snapshot, a title from raw lines, an opener/closer model, and now give-back state. Each fix was correct and each revealed another case. A real block parser, or a vendored minimal one, would replace the whole surface.

Narrow D1 to what has never been destructive: strip HTML comments only, with no fence awareness at all. That reopens the 'comment inside a fenced example' case Codex found in attempt two, so it is a deliberate trade, not a fix.

escalation.executor_note: Nine attempts across four packages, two withdrawn with budgets exhausted. My recommendation is A first and B if A does not hold, and I would not authorise a further attempt inside chunk_note's current shape without one of them.
